The Story of Jinmati

I bow to Lord Jinendra, who is worshipped by the gods of heaven, and I write the story of Jinmati, who did not abandon right faith.

In the famous city of Galagrodh in Latadesh, there lived a merchant named Jindatt. His wife was Jindatta. They had a daughter named Jinmati. Jinmati was very beautiful. Seeing her world-enchanting beauty, even the celestial nymphs of heaven were ashamed. Beauty is attained through merit.

In the same city lived another merchant named Nagdatt. Nagdatt's wife Nagdatta had a son named Rudradatt. Nagdatt tried hard to have Jindatt give Jinmati in marriage to his son Rudradatt. But being of a different faith, Jindatt did not give his daughter to him. Jindatt's stubbornness displeased Nagdatt. So he devised another strategy. Nagdatt and Rudradatt took some vows from Samadhi Gupt Muni and became shravakas, performing all the activities of laymen. Jindatt was very pleased by this. He became fully convinced that they had truly become Jains. So he happily gave Jinmati in marriage to Rudradatt.

As soon as the marriage took place, both father and son abandoned Jain dharma and returned to their own faith. Rudradatt now began to insist daily that Jinmati also adopt his faith, saying, 'My dear, why don't you adopt my faith? It is a very superior faith.'

Jinmati had deep faith in Jain dharma. She was a true servant of Lord Jinendra. In such a state, how could any faith other than Jain dharma appeal to her? She then expressed her views very freely to her husband. She said, 'My lord, whatever your faith may be, I have nothing to say or hear about it. But according to my faith, I will say that in this world, Jain dharma alone can claim to be supreme. For it is capable of benefiting all living beings, and great kings, gods of heaven, Vidyadharas, and Chakravartins all worship and honour it. Nor do I find any unreasonable thing in it that would compel me to abandon it. Rather, I would advise you too to adopt this true faith that benefits all living beings — Jain dharma.'

Rudradatt was angered by her words and tried to force her to change her faith. But Jinmati remained steadfast. She endured all manner of pressure and hardship but never wavered from her faith. Her unwavering devotion to Jain dharma eventually inspired even her husband to reconsider his own beliefs.

This story teaches that true faith cannot be shaken by any amount of pressure, even from one's own husband. Jinmati's steadfastness in the face of her husband's demands shows the power of genuine spiritual conviction. The wise should cultivate such firm faith that no worldly relationship can compel them to abandon it.
